mainTopic: The threshold (אסקופה) in the laws of carrying: resting in a מקום פטור, the open/locked rule of אחרים and the לחי problem, and a 10×4 threshold as its own domain
overview: This amud picks up in the middle of a challenge. Based on רבא, the גמרא argued that passing an object through a מקום פטור does not split the act of carrying. The גמרא answers that an object that only passes through the air is different from one that actually comes to rest in the מקום פטור. Next it quotes אחרים in the תוספתא: a threshold counts as inside when the door is open and as outside when the door is locked. The גמרא challenges this with רב's rule that a doorway needs its own לחי, even if it is smaller than four by four טפחים. רב then explains that the case is a half-roofed threshold of a מבוי. רב אשי explains it as a house threshold roofed with two narrow beams joined by לבוד, with the door between them. Finally, the תוספתא says a threshold ten טפחים high and four wide is a domain by itself. This supports רבי מאיר's decree against resting a load on such a pillar inside a רשות היחיד, made because of a mound in a רשות הרבים.

steps.title: End of the challenge: passing above the ground still makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting רבא: someone who carries four אמות in רשות הרבים is חייב even if the object passed through the air above, which is a מקום פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: This line ends a challenge that began on the previous amud. רבא ruled that carrying four אמות in רשות הרבים makes a person liable even if the object traveled through the air above ten טפחים, which is a מקום פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תוספתא implied that passing an object through a מקום פטור (the threshold) breaks the act apart, so the person is פטור. רבא's ruling seems to say the opposite: going through a מקום פטור does not break the act, and the person is still חייב. So the two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: By way of the space above it, through the air above the ground
Liable (here, for a Torah-level act of carrying)
An exempt area that is not a real domain for the laws of carrying

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'דרך עליו חייב' are the punchline of a challenge that began earlier. They are not a new statement.

phrases.english: by way of above it — he is liable!
phrases.notes: The end of רבא's ruling, used as a challenge to the תוספתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea from the תוספתא that passing through a מקום פטור exempts the carrier.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא holds that passing through a מקום פטור (the air above ten טפחים) does not break the act of carrying, so the person is liable. That seems to contradict the exemption given for the threshold.

steps.title: Resting versus merely passing through
steps.stepSummary: In רבא's case the object never landed in the מקום פטור. In the threshold case it did land, and that breaks the act of carrying into two parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it did not come to rest. Here, it came to rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing out a difference between the two cases. In רבא's case the object only flew through the exempt air, but on the threshold the object actually came to rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Passing through a מקום פטור by itself does not break up the act. Coming to rest (הנחה) in a מקום פטור does break it up. That turns it into two separate small acts, and neither one is a full Torah-level act of carrying.
steps.whatToRemember: Passing an object through a מקום פטור does not cancel liability. Resting the object in a מקום פטור does split the act into two.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a basic rule of הוצאה: what matters is where the object comes to rest (הנחה), not just the path it travels.

phrases.english: There, it did not come to rest;
phrases.notes: רבא's case: the object only passed through the air.

phrases.english: here, it came to rest.
phrases.notes: The threshold case: the object landed in the מקום פטור.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any passage through a מקום פטור should be treated the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only resting (הנחה) in a מקום פטור breaks up the act of carrying. Passing through it does not.

steps.title: אחרים: the threshold serves two domains
steps.stepSummary: אחרים in the תוספתא say the threshold counts as inside the house when the door is open and as outside when the door is locked.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: A threshold serves two domains. When the door is open, it is like the inside. When the door is locked, it is like the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the תוספתא, which is the opinion of אחרים. They say the status of the threshold changes depending on whether the door is open or locked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the door is open, the threshold is joined to the house and counts as רשות היחיד. When the door is locked, the door cuts the threshold off from the house, so it belongs with the outside. This statement sets up the questions that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', an anonymous תנא, often identified as רבי מאיר

phrases.english: Others say:
a threshold serves two domains:
when the doorway is open — it is like the inside.
phrases.notes: It counts as part of the house, a רשות היחיד.

phrases.english: When the doorway is locked — it is like the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same תוספתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The status of the threshold depends on the door: open means it counts as inside (רשות היחיד), locked means it counts as outside.

steps.title: Doesn't a doorway need its own post?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אחרים: how can the threshold count as inside without a לחי, when רב said a doorway needs an additional לחי to permit carrying there?
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though it has no post?! But didn't רב חמא בר גוריא say in the name of רב: The space inside the doorway needs another post to permit it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first half of the statement of אחרים, that an open doorway counts as inside. It quotes רב, who says the doorway space needs its own לחי before one may carry there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the space within a doorway is not automatically part of the permitted area. It needs an extra לחי. The תוספתא makes the threshold 'like inside' without mentioning any לחי, so it seems to contradict רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A post set at the side of an opening that serves as a symbolic partition
'But didn't he say', a formula that opens a challenge

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ לֶחִי?!
phrases.english: And even though it does not have a post?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chama bar Gurya say that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹךְ הַפֶּתַח צָרִיךְ לֶחִי אַחֵר לְהַתִּירוֹ!
phrases.english: the space inside the doorway requires another post to permit it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ לֶחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'open door = inside' clause from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of אחרים that an open threshold counts as inside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב requires an extra לחי for the doorway space, but the תוספתא allows it with no לחי.

steps.title: Suggestion: the threshold is smaller than four by four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the תוספתא is talking about a threshold smaller than four by four טפחים, which might not need a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it does not have an area of four by four…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer: perhaps the threshold in the תוספתא is too small to count as its own area. It does not stop here, because it is about to reject this answer in the very next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An area smaller than four by four טפחים is usually too small to have its own status. The idea is that such a small threshold would simply belong with the house, so it would not need a לחי, and רב's rule would not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say', which introduces a suggested answer
Four by four טפחים, the minimum size to count as a significant area

phrases.english: And if you say that it does not have
four by four handbreadths —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a small threshold
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The threshold in the תוספתא is a full-sized area that should need a לחי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps it is smaller than four by four, so it needs no לחי. (This is rejected next.)

steps.title: Objection: רב requires a post even for a small doorway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion by quoting רב again: even without four by four טפחים, the doorway space needs another לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב חמא בר גוריא say in the name of רב: The space inside the doorway, even though it does not have four by four, needs another post to permit it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggested answer. רב explicitly said that size does not matter here: even a small doorway space needs a לחי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'small threshold' answer depended on the idea that a small area needs no לחי. רב's second statement directly cancels that idea. So the challenge against אחרים still stands until Steps 7 and 8 give new answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though it does not have

steps.confusionAlert: רב חמא בר גוריא is quoting רב twice, with two different statements. The second one adds the words 'even without four by four' in order to block the suggested answer.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chama bar Gurya say that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹךְ הַפֶּתַח, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ
phrases.english: the space inside the doorway, even though it does not have
four by four handbreadths,
requires another post to permit it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב תּוֹךְ הַפֶּתַח אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested answer from step 5, which brings back the challenge from step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire 'smaller than four by four' answer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב explicitly requires a לחי even when the doorway space is smaller than four by four, so size cannot be the way out.

steps.title: רב Explains the Case as an Alleyway Threshold
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says the תוספתא is talking about the threshold of a מבוי that is half roofed, with the roofing on the inner side. When the entrance is open, the threshold counts as inside. When it is locked, it counts as outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Here we are dealing with the threshold of an alleyway. Half of it is roofed and half is not, and the roofing is on the inner side. If the entrance is open, the threshold is like the inside. If the entrance is locked, it is like the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to save the תוספתא of אחרים. It moves the case from a house to an alleyway (מבוי).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the roofing does the work that a לחי would otherwise do, so רב's demand for an extra לחי in the doorway no longer causes a problem. When the entrance is open, the edge of the roofing over the inner half acts like a wall coming down (פי תקרה יורד וסותם), which closes off the alleyway and makes the threshold part of the inside. When the entrance is locked, the roofing can no longer be treated as a partition, so the part of the threshold beyond the locked door counts as outside.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway that houses open into, closed on three sides
The threshold at the entrance of the alleyway

steps.confusionAlert: This is still the same תוספתא of אחרים (open is inside, locked is outside). רב is not giving a new ruling. He is only changing which kind of threshold the ruling is about, so that it avoids the problem with the לחי.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Here we are dealing with the threshold of an alleyway,
half of it roofed and half of it not roofed,
phrases.notes: Only part of the threshold is under the roof.

phrases.english: and its roofing is toward the inside.
If the entrance is open, it is like the inside.
phrases.notes: The edge of the roof is treated as a wall coming down.

phrases.english: If the entrance is locked, it is like the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after Step 6 rejected the 'less than four טפחים' answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the case (אוקימתא): an alleyway threshold instead of a house threshold
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תוספתא is about a house threshold, so it would need an extra לחי according to רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תוספתא is about a half-roofed alleyway threshold. The roofing's edge counts as a wall when the entrance is open, so no extra לחי is needed.

steps.title: רב אשי Explains the Case as a House Threshold with Two Beams
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי keeps the case as a house threshold. He says it is roofed by two beams, each less than four טפחים wide, with less than three טפחים between them, and a door in the middle. When the door is open the beams join into one roof, so the threshold is inside. When the door is locked they do not join, so the outer part is outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really, we are dealing with the threshold of a house. The case is where someone roofed it with two beams. Neither beam is four טפחים wide, the gap between them is less than three טפחים, and the door is in the middle. If the entrance is open, it is like the inside. If the entrance is locked, it is like the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer. He keeps the house threshold but describes a very specific roofing setup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the gap is less than three טפחים, the rule of לבוד treats it as closed, so the two beams count as one wide roof. That roof's edge then counts as a wall coming down. When the door is shut it divides the beams, and the outer beam alone is less than four טפחים wide. It is too narrow to count as a roof, so the area under it counts as outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (we keep the original assumption)
A gap of less than three טפחים is treated as closed
A door standing between the two beams

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Actually, we are dealing with the threshold of a house,
in a case where he roofed it with two beams

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין בָּזוֹ אַרְבָּעָה וְאֵין בָּזוֹ אַרְבָּעָה,
phrases.english: where this one is not four (טפחים wide) and that one is not four,
and there are not three (טפחים) between this one and that one,
phrases.notes: Less than three, so the rule of לבוד joins the beams.

phrases.english: and the door is in the middle.
If the entrance is open, it is like the inside.
phrases.notes: The beams join into one roof at least four wide.

phrases.english: If the entrance is locked, it is like the outside.
phrases.notes: The closed door separates the beams, so the outer beam is too narrow to count as a roof.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם בְּאִיסְקוּפַּת בַּיִת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same problem that Step 7 answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the case (אוקימתא): a house threshold with special roofing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A house threshold cannot count as inside without an extra לחי.
steps.terutzMaskana: With two beams joined by לבוד and a door between them, the roof counts as a wall when the door is open. That makes the threshold inside without a לחי.

steps.title: A High, Wide Threshold Is Its Own Domain
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא continues: if the threshold is ten טפחים high and four wide, it counts as a separate domain of its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the threshold was ten טפחים high and four טפחים wide, it is a domain by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the same תוספתא. This line sets up the support for רב יצחק בר אבדימי in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten high and four by four wide are the measurements of a רשות היחיד. So a threshold this size gets its own status. It is not swept into the house or the outside, even if the door is open.

phrases.english: And if the threshold was
ten (טפחים) high and four wide,
it is a domain by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיְתָה אִיסְקוּפָּה גְּבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה וּרְחָבָה אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the תוספתא of Step 3 and quotes its next clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A threshold ten טפחים high and four wide is its own domain.

steps.title: The תוספתא Supports רבי מאיר's Rule About a Pillar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this line supports רב יצחק בר אבדימי. He reported that רבי מאיר said: when there are two areas that are each a domain but really are one domain, such as a pillar ten by four inside a רשות היחיד, one may not rest a load on the pillar. This is a decree because of a mound in the רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב יצחק בר אבדימי, who said that רבי מאיר used to say: Any place where you find two domains that are really one domain, like a pillar in a private domain that is ten טפחים high and four wide, it is forbidden to adjust a load on it. This is a decree because of a mound in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the תוספתא's line about a separate domain backs up a teaching of רב יצחק בר אבדימי. It then quotes that teaching in full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pillar inside a private domain is also private by מדאורייתא, so moving things onto it should be fine. רבי מאיר still forbids it, because people might do the same with a mound in the public domain, where it would be real carrying. The תוספתא calling a high threshold 'a domain by itself' matches this idea: a raised 10×4 spot gets its own status even when it sits within a private area.

keyTerms.meaning: To rest or adjust a load on one's shoulder
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

steps.confusionAlert: The pillar really is a רשות היחיד, the same kind of domain as the area around it. The ban is only a rabbinic decree. It is not a Torah prohibition.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to save the תוספתא from רב's לחי problem. רב sets it in a half-roofed alleyway. רב אשי sets it in a house with two beams joined by לבוד. A threshold ten by four is its own domain, which supports רבי מאיר's decree against using a pillar in a רשות היחיד, made because of a mound in a רשות הרבים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that חז"ל sometimes forbid an act that is allowed by Torah law, because it looks just like an act that is forbidden by Torah law.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי.
phrases.english: This supports Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi.
For Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi said:
Rabbi Meir used to say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא שְׁתֵּי רְשׁוּיוֹת
phrases.english: Any place where you find two domains
and they are really one domain,
for example, a pillar in a private domain
ten (טפחים) high and four wide —
it is forbidden to adjust a load on it.
It is a decree because of a mound in the public domain.
phrases.notes: Placing something on such a mound in the public domain would be Torah-level carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the תוספתא line from Step 9 as support for a report of an אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: רב יצחק בר אבדימי's report that רבי מאיר forbade resting a load on a 10×4 pillar inside a רשות היחיד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תוספתא: a threshold ten high and four wide is 'a domain by itself'
